findings.change: One resource-cell transition machine owns delivery generation, authority epoch, latest refresh nonce and captured attempt key. Latest refresh blocks new dispatch; completion reads current snapshot and only changes its captured attempt under matching generation/epoch/nonce. Old metadata or ignored transport cannot clear a later pending/uncertain/failure or undo a newer denial. Parent permission revalidation also fences scope/epoch and requires a fresh successful read identity; history refresh checks current token before and after waits.
findings.proof: Actual held parent A history/B permissions+history/C registration sequence remains one exact key/body after lost C response. Older refresh under new authority403 cannot restore controls; pure machine tests assert stale nonce/delivery/epoch no-ops and retire behavior. No raw secret snapshot retained.

findings.change: Strict receipt codec selected from dispatched action before resolving unknown outcome. Destination registration cannot accept a policy receipt. Grant requires revision1; update exact input policyRevision+1 and known policy ID; revoke follows actual already-revoked same revision vs next revision; policy mutation receipts require operationID and literal revocationEffective=false. Manual revision is source-bound between original admission read and current known policy read because the native command has no policyRevision fence. Wrong-action/malformed/foreign/unconfirmed revision after send stays ambiguous with original key/digest/metadata.
findings.proof: Actual parent lost-register/exact-retry→policy receipt, malformed destination and update destination/foreign/same/higher revision cases stay unknown and reuse original key.
